description: Five-panel composite of bright-field optical micrographs of hot-rolled Fe-Al alloys, apparently etched, all showing the annealed microstructure; panel (a) carries the only printed scale bar, labelled 250µm, in the bottom-right corner, and panels (b)-(e) show no scale bar, axis, legend or numeric label. All panels show coarse, equiaxed, fully recrystallised grains containing straight closely spaced parallel bands interpreted as annealing twins, together with dark rounded dots interpreted as residual porosity/second-phase particles. (a) AIM 7 wt.% Al: very coarse polygonal grains, a few twin lamellae, scattered pores. (b) AIMFC 7 wt.% Al: somewhat smaller, more uniform grains densely decorated with dark dots both inside grains and along boundaries. (c) AIMFC 9 wt.% Al: large grains with moderate dark pitting and clear grain boundaries. (d) VIM 7 wt.% Al: equiaxed grains with prominent twin lamellae and dotted particles. (e) VIM 9 wt.% Al: the coarsest grains in the group, with strongly developed parallel twin-boundary bands. Together the panels demonstrate that the AIM, AIMFC and VIM melting routes all yield a coarse-grained, annealed structure after hot rolling.

observations.observation: Panel (a) contains a printed scale bar reading "250µm" in its bottom-right corner; panels (b)-(e) carry no visible scale bar.
All five panels show a coarse, equiaxed, fully recrystallised single-phase-looking grain structure, consistent with an annealed condition after hot rolling.
Straight, closely spaced parallel lines inside many grains, characteristic of annealing twins, are visible in panels (a), (d) and (e), and to a lesser degree in (c).
Dark rounded dots (pores or particles) are distributed inside grains and along grain boundaries, most densely in panel (b) and least in panel (a).
Panel (e) contains the largest grains of the group, whereas panel (b) contains the smallest and most uniformly sized grains.
The caption identifies the panels as optical micrographs of hot-rolled Fe-Al alloys containing (a) AIM 7 wt.% Al, (b) AIMFC 7 wt.% Al, (c) AIMFC 9 wt.% Al, (d) VIM 7 wt.% Al, and (e) VIM 9 wt.% Al.
The citing text states that all alloys produced by the AIM, AIMFC and VIM processes exhibited an annealed microstructure with coarse grain size (Fig. 4).
The citing text states that the grain size of all alloys produced by AIMFC is comparable with the grain size of alloys produced by the VIM process (Table II).
The citing text states that AIM ingots containing 9 wt.% Al could not be thermomechanically processed because of gas porosity, so no AIM 9 wt.% Al micrograph appears in this five-panel group.

The citing text states that the hot-rolled plates contained microcracks attributed to a high residual hydrogen level in the as-cast ingots; the photomicrographs do not clearly resolve such cracks at the supplied resolution.
The processing route given in the citing text is 1373 K preheat for 1 h, hot forging, then hot rolling by 50% to a 12 mm final plate thickness, which is the condition of the samples shown.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph, AIM 7 wt.% Al hot-rolled alloy; very coarse equiaxed grains with a few straight parallel twin bands and scattered dark pores. Only this panel has a printed scale bar, labelled 250µm (bottom right).

Optical micrograph, AIMFC 7 wt.% Al hot-rolled alloy; relatively smaller, more uniform grains densely decorated with dark dots (pores/particles) within grains and along grain boundaries. No scale bar printed.
Optical micrograph, AIMFC 9 wt.% Al hot-rolled alloy; large polygonal grains with moderately pitted interiors and clearly delineated boundaries. No scale bar printed.
Optical micrograph, VIM 7 wt.% Al hot-rolled alloy; equiaxed grains with prominent straight annealing-twin lamellae and dotted dark particles. No scale bar printed.
Optical micrograph, VIM 9 wt.% Al hot-rolled alloy; the coarsest grains of the group with strongly developed parallel twin-boundary bands. No scale bar printed.

unreadable_items: panels (b)-(e): no scale bar printed, so their magnification cannot be confirmed from the images
the dark dots cannot be resolved as gas porosity versus second-phase particles from the micrographs alone
individual grain-boundary cracks mentioned in the citing text are not clearly identifiable in any panel at the supplied resolution
